prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows a sloped outdoor grassy ground plane stretching away from the camera wearer across frames 1–3, with a black dog in the foreground at roughly 1.5–2 m in front, a husky-type dog behind and to the right moving from roughly 3–4 m in frames 1–2 to about 2–2.5 m in frame 3, and a third white dog entering the bottom-right foreground at about 1–1.5 m (nearly within arm's reach) in frame 3. Another person's legs are visible in the upper-right background of frames 2–3 at roughly 4–5 m away, while in frames 4–5 the camera pitches downward and rotates rapidly, bringing the wearer's own legs, a held cup/container in the right hand (within 0.5 m), a low wooden bench edge on the bottom left, and the husky's head at the bottom-left corner (about 1 m away) into close range. Relative to RGB, the depth map clearly separates the foreground black dog's silhouette from the dark, muddy ground where its dark fur blends in, and confirms the relative depth ordering of the three dogs and background person in frame 3. However, the depth map becomes highly unreliable during the severe motion blur of frame 4—where the ground and moving black dog dissolve into an indistinct dark/light smudge—and in frame 5, where the distant person on the upper-left walkway is completely lost in the dark background.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates discrete foreground entities in frames 1–3, showing the black dog in the centre-left foreground (~1.5–2 m away, facing right in frame 1 and turning toward the camera wearer in frames 2–3) and the husky behind it (~2–4 m away, moving left-to-right and approaching the wearer in frame 3) separated by about 1.5–2 m from each other. In frames 2–3, it also segments the partially occluded person at the top-right edge (~4–5 m away, facing roughly toward the scene with only their lower body/torso in view) and the white dog entering at the bottom right (~1–1.5 m away, facing left toward the husky) in frame 3. In frame 4, only a small yellow object on the ground/near the wearer's hand is segmented, and in frame 5 no masks are produced at all despite the wearer's right leg, the husky's head at the bottom-left bench, and a distant person at the upper left being present in RGB. While segmentation helps distinguish overlapping contours—such as the black dog partially occluding the husky in frame 1 and the husky adjacent to the white dog in frame 3—it is severely unreliable in class labelling and recall: it misclassifies the black dog as a 'bear' in frames 2–3, the white dog as a 'bird' in frame 3, and a yellow leaf/object as a 'banana' in frame 4, while completely missing all objects, dogs, and body parts in frames 4 and 5.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is completely blank (all black) across all five frames, failing to render any yellow body skeletons or magenta hand skeletons despite multiple human body parts appearing in the RGB strip. Specifically, in RGB, a standing person is partially visible at the upper-right edge at roughly 4–5 m away in frames 2–3 (with their torso and legs in frame 2 and only legs in frame 3, facing toward the dogs) and another distant person is visible at the upper-left walkway (~6–8 m away) in frame 5. In addition, the camera wearer's own blue-jeaned legs and right hand holding a white stacked cup within arm's reach (~0.3–0.5 m below the camera) appear at the bottom of frames 4 and 5 as the camera looks downward. Because the pose estimator requires sufficient unoccluded human keypoints and fails on heavily cropped limbs, distant figures, and motion-blurred egocentric views, the pose map provides no spatial information that is not better seen in RGB and is completely unreliable throughout this sequence.
